proof:
Let $P_j$ be the vertices and let $t_{ij}=v_i\cdot(P_j-y)$, $Q_i=q_i/k$, and $S_i=\sigma_i/k$. Let $R_{ij}$ be the captured length fraction on the edge opposite $P_j$. Apply the divergence theorem to $x-P_j$ on cap $i$. The divergence is two, its flux on edges incident to $P_j$ is zero, the opposite edge flux is $2kR_{ij}$, and the cut flux is $t_{ij}\sigma_i$, using the outward normal $-v_i/\lVert v_i\rVert$. Thus $R_{ij}=Q_i-t_{ij}S_i/2$. This includes vertex-level sections, since edges of the clipped polygon and their fluxes give the same identity and isolated points have zero length.

Define $X_{ij}=R_{ij}/(S_iM)$ and $a_i=Q_i/(S_iM)$. The entries are nonnegative and their column sums are one because $\sum_iQ_i/S_i=M$ and $\sum_i t_{ij}=0$. Also $t_{ij}=2M(a_i-X_{ij})$. For uniform barycentric $\Xi$ the cap is the event $X_i\cdot\Xi\le a_i$. Its distribution function $G_i$ satisfies $G_i(a_i)=Q_i$ and $G'_i(a_i)=2MS_i$. Indeed the original raw normal at that threshold has section coarea $S_i$, and the affine row evaluates to $a_i-v_i\cdot(x-y)/(2M)$. The threshold is interior to the projection interval because $y$ is interior, and its section length is continuous there, including at a vertex level. Consequently $a_i G_i'(a_i)=2Q_i$.

By planar Brunn–Minkowski for nested convex sublevel caps, $\sqrt{G_i(c)}$ is concave on the projection interval and remains so under its constant continuation above the upper endpoint. At $a_i$ its tangent is the line through the origin with slope $\sqrt{Q_i}/a_i$. Therefore the infimum of $c/\sqrt{G_i(c)}$ over positive-mass positive thresholds is attained at $a_i$. The uniform-triangle-exact-row-capacity formula identifies this infimum with $\sqrt{F(X_i)}$ from three-by-three-column-stochastic-cubic, and $f_i=2a_i/\sqrt{Q_i}=2\sqrt{F(X_i)}$. The matrix cubic gives the asserted bound after multiplying by four.

Here every $f_i>0$. The equality criterion of the stochastic cubic requires a permutation of columns with diagonal zero. An edge has captured length fraction zero exactly when neither of its endpoints is strictly captured, because a proper interior cut cannot contain an entire triangle edge. Thus a row zero corresponds to a unique strictly captured vertex opposite that edge. The diagonal criterion gives the three distinct captured vertices, and with them matched to the diagonal labels the rows of $X$ have the form $(0,u_1,1-u_2)$, $(1-u_3,0,u_2)$, $(u_3,1-u_1,0)$. The exact equality test is $\prod_i u_i=\prod_i(1-u_i)$. For example the three cuts $\xi_i\ge1/3$ at the triangle centroid have balanced spanning barycentric normals and, by affine symmetry, off-diagonal normalized fractions $1/2$.

Finally $0<f_i<2$ by positivity of the other terms in the cubic. For $g=f_j+f_l$, use $f_jf_l\le g^2/4$ to obtain
$$
4\ge f_i^2+g^2-(2-f_i)f_jf_l\ge f_i^2+(2+f_i)g^2/4.
$$
Division by $2+f_i$ gives the row bound, with equality precisely as stated.

statement:
Let $K$ be a nondegenerate planar triangle with interior point $y$ and nonzero spanning normals $v_1,v_2,v_3$ with $v_1+v_2+v_3=0$. Let $q_i$ be the area of $K\cap\{v_i\cdot(x-y)\ge0\}$ and $\sigma_i$ the length of its cutting section divided by $\lVert v_i\rVert$. Put $k=|K|$, $M=\sum_iq_i/\sigma_i$, and $f_i=2\sqrt{kq_i}/(\sigma_i M)$. Then
$$
\sum_i f_i^2+f_1f_2f_3\le4,\qquad
f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4\le2\quad(\{i,j,l\}=\{1,2,3\}).
$$
The cubic is strict if one cap strictly captures two vertices. In general equality holds precisely when the caps each have one strictly captured vertex, those vertices are distinct, and the three off-diagonal column splits of the normalized edge fractions defined in the proof have equal forward and backward products. Equality in an individual row bound further requires $f_j=f_l$.
title: Cubic inequality for every balanced through-point triple on an ordinary triangle
